trigger.snippet: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `evidence` line names the evidence directory, its size and `evidence.budget`, and warns once the directory has reached the budget, since a valid miss then keeps no more until `evidence.budget` is raised in the configuration; `melian store prune` keeps evidence until [issue #633](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/633) lands. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. The same line then says whom the committed root policy trusts to write the branch. It reads `trust.writers` from the same base as the `trust` line. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's writers. With it off, it warns that only the trusted host may write `melian/state`, since doctor cannot check who may push to it. When no policy can be read, it warns that who may write the branch is unknown. A policy read from local `main` or `HEAD` makes the line a warning, with the `trust` line's caveat. Doctor reads the cached remote-tracking ref and never fetches it. So a clone that has not fetched reports the policy as of its last fetch, and each of the two lines names the ref and commit it read. [Issue #491](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/491) would check that commit against the remote. It never pushes and never fails. It also checks the named credentials of the secrets files, failing when git tracks `melian.local.yaml` or `melian.secrets.yaml` or a secrets file cannot be read, and warning for one others can read. It checks whether each lens's levels cost more from `quick` to `deep`, warning for a level on a lighter tier or with a smaller token or tool budget than the level below it. Its `resolution` lines list, for each `melian.yaml` and preference file in the working tree, every farther value and lens default its `resolution` overrides, or say that none does. It checks whether Biome and tsc come from the checkout or Melian's own copy. Its `packages` line reads Melian's own install. It warns, naming each place, when a link leaves the install or a place is not laid out as npm lays out an install, since no review then reuses a run, and fails when the install cannot be read. Its `probes` line runs an empty probe and says whether probes run here, or why every probe is refused, as a warning. When probes run, it then runs a probe that calls `git init`, and reads `run under sandbox-runtime, git included` when git runs there, or warns with git's own reason when it does not, since a probe that calls git would then fail. Each manifest tool has a readiness line: materialised and verified, not yet fetched, unavailable, or manifest mismatch. `unavailable` marks a platform with no pin or a cache path that cannot be inspected, and doctor reports it as a warning. Doctor never downloads or runs a manifest tool; a mismatch fails doctor. Its standards line counts regular standards files and their bytes at every depth, warns for oversized files and skipped symlinks, and lists at most ten paths. Its `decision index` line gives the size of the decision index at `HEAD`, and warns past 64 KiB, with the warning `melian review` gives, or when the decisions cannot be read; it never fails. Its `routes` line names each tier’s resolved provider/model route and status, including the verifier. It also prints the review plan it would resolve now, as `plan` lines, from the working tree and the preference files. A pull request's review reads its policy and lenses from its base and no preference file. So a `plan` warning names each preference file doctor read, and every key it sets, from the loader's own list. It leaves out `output`, which every review reads from the preference files to render. Problem: on [pull request #532](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/532) a lens route in `melian.local.yaml` printed as applying. Two pull request rounds ran on the committed model before anyone knew. Doctor takes no pull request argument and never fetches, so it cannot print a pull request's own plan. The warning is what it can say. Each routed tier shows its models, the credential each comes from, and the file that routed it, or that it was derived. Each lens's levels show the tier and model of each, and a lens with its own route has a `route` line and shows each level on the lens route. Every warning appears too. A tier with no route names the lenses that use it and the ways to fix it. Other warnings name missing credentials, a tier policy refuses, a route off the committed one, or a route model the catalogue does not hold, with the file that set it and, for an unknown provider, the provider. It fails with its own `decisions` line when `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider` | `0`, or `1` when Node or git cannot run a review, `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider`, git tracks a file only a maintainer may hold, a secrets file cannot be read, or a named credential's provider is unknown or accepts neither API keys nor OAuth tokens, a manifest tool mismatches its pin, or Melian's install cannot be read |

The caller section and the Enola graph its tools read, under `bestEffort`, since a host whose graph query failed would otherwise rerun every lens. The preference file's path in the standards' source, which names the host. Who set the route, and the credential, by [the run identity decision](../decisions/2026-11-08-lens-run-identity.md). The key holds the run under the fixed nonce, its route, thinking, level, budgets, instructions and prompt with the enclosing functions, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-14; the injection policy and the name of the section Pi renders it in. It holds `packages`, the digest of Melian's whole install, and `identified`, whether Melian could identify that install, by [the decision of 2026-11-20](../decisions/2026-11-20-keys-hold-installed-packages.md), so a run on an install it can identify never attaches to one made on an install it cannot with the same digest. That install holds Pi Durable and pi-ai, which render the system prompt and turns and write them into each provider's request. It holds every tool offered by name, description, schema, output limits and argument bound, and the bounds every lens tool cuts what it shows to, `lensToolLimits`. It holds both failover wordings, `handoverWording`, the one that continues earlier work and the one that starts afresh, since a conversation's history picks between them at run time. It holds a probing run's tools; base, head, `escalateAt` and the escalation; and the standards by text, source and trust. A lens with `standards: false` keys no standards text, only their source and trust, so turning a lens's standards off asks its runs again once, by [the decision of 2026-11-19](../decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md). As a lens record's key, it lets `melian records relay` take a lens run's early copy, with no check, beside a round that reads a lens record under the same key, by [issue #397](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/397). For a run that probes, it holds the probing wording its planner and prober read: the shared lines, and the entries in core's `lensProbingWording` of its lens's `probesAs`, or of its own name. So a change to one lens's words asks no other lens's run again. [Issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) changed the trust-boundary lens's probing wording on purpose, so its probing runs are asked again once. For a run that escalates to another, it holds the shared lines, which carry its findings on, by rule 8 and [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md). For a run offered `list_mutants`, the key holds the instrumenter that answers it, `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](../decisions/2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md). It holds its version, read from the `package.json` of the package the tool resolves, and `packages`, the digest of the whole install the instrumenter resolves from, Babel included, with whether it is identified. It holds its source, the checkout's install or Melian's, or `unavailable` when neither resolves. A run not offered the tool keys nothing more. A probing run's environment names its host by one value, `probingHost`, whose architecture and Node version come from core's `hostFacts`: the sandbox's platform and kind, the installed sandbox-runtime release, read from its own `package.json`, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probe. Left out of that value: the operating system's release, since the platform names the system, and the CPU's model, since the architecture names the instruction set Node runs. Also left out: whether the filesystem folds case, since a probing run is reused only from its own checkout's store, so a temporary directory moved to a volume that folds differently copies a run probed under the other rule. So are the host's locale and clock, which no probe should hang on. A probing run's environment holds the base policy's `probe.conditions` when it names any, since a condition changes which file a bare import loads, and holds nothing for an empty list, so a request asked before the key had conditions keeps its key. `probingHost` holds the kind and the version of each program a probe can run that the host supplies, and nothing else of the host, by [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-22-probes-run-git-and-workspace-imports.md#keys). On macOS it also holds `git`, the kind of the host's git lookup, `linked`, or `linked-no-system` where git runs with no system configuration, and `gitVersion`, git's whole trimmed answer to `--version`, at most 200 characters. It leaves both fields out where git is unavailable, as it was on every host before probes could run git, and on Linux, so those runs keep their keys; a run made before git could run is reused only where git is still unavailable. The fields keep no path: where the developer tools' git lives names the host's install, as the read paths do. The system git configuration is a host file a probe reads, not a program it runs, so it stays out, and git's kind records whether it exists. Tests: `probing.test.ts` checks each kind with its version and the absent fields, and refuses a probe planned under another git kind or release; `probing-level.test.ts` checks that a change of kind alone probes again, a change of version alone probes again, a change of paths alone does not, and a host whose git is unavailable keys the five fields it keyed before; `probe-git.test.ts` checks the version's bound at 200 characters and one past it. Left out of the request, by [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md): what Melian's probe runner gives a probe and what `run_probe` returns, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437), so a release that changes them copies a run probed under the old code. Also left out: what the read paths hold, the installed dependencies of the code under test among them, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so a reinstall between two reviews of one head copies the run and its conclusive reruns. A task stored before the key, lens task version 6, holds no request key, so nothing is copied from it and the first review after the upgrade runs every lens once. The lens tools' own code, `list_mutants`'s included, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15: the text each tool returns to the model, what each tool does, and the lens extension's code, which the key cannot hold as data. Rule 8 forbids hashing source at run time, so [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) ties a code version to a hash of them in a test; until then a change there reuses runs asked under the old code. Chord, Pi's composition runtime, which shows a model nothing. `packages` holds one entry for each copy, `[place, "manifest", sha256 of its package.json bytes]` or `[place, "no manifest"]`, and one for each link, `[place, "links", target]`, hashed as core's `canonicalJson` of the sorted entries, in every `node_modules` tree Node searches beneath the install root, read by `Install.read` with no link followed. Two installs with one digest hold the same manifest, hashed whole, and link at every place, so every import reaches the same release. Any install change asks every lens again once, a dev dependency's included, about $5 of tokens a full round here. Left out: every file of a package but its manifest, such as a patched file, postinstall output, a native binary or another tarball under one version, a `node_modules` beneath the root that no walked tree holds, and CommonJS's global folders. A link out of the install keys a fixed entry and leaves the install unidentified, as a layout other than npm's does: Yarn's Plug'n'Play map, a module read through an archive, a walked directory named as one, a directory reached as two kinds of place, or a module beneath a `node_modules` that no keyed package holds. `runLenses` then neither attaches nor copies, so no run is reused. Past 50,000 directories, the walk of Melian's install, or the instrumenter's, stops reading there, and the install is unidentified. A directory or manifest the walk cannot read leaves the install unidentified, and a manifest is keyed by its bytes unparsed. Tests in `installed-packages.test.ts`: the seven layouts that collided under earlier forms, an npm alias and a changed `exports`, `main` or `type`, each told apart, and each file the key leaves out; each unrecognised layout, and the installed, pnpm and workspace modules recognised; one layout at two absolute paths giving one digest; links outside and the bound, in both its forms. Tests elsewhere: a moved package Pi never imports changes the key, in `lens-request.test.ts`; an unidentified install, Melian's or the instrumenter's, reuses no lens run, and a review on an identified install asks every lens again after one on an unidentified install with the same digest, in `lens-reuse-review.test.ts`. The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) |

snippet.text: - Reads only of the head's tracked tree, the dependency install, Node's install, sandbox-runtime's own package, and the operating system's programs and libraries: `/bin`, `/sbin`, and `/usr`'s `bin`, `sbin`, `lib*`, `libexec` and `share`, with `/System` and `/private/var/select` on macOS and `/lib*` on Linux. Node does not start without its libraries and OpenSSL configuration, a shell needs its own, and Linux runs sandbox-runtime's seccomp helper from its package; the maintainer accepted these reads on 2026-11-07. On macOS `/usr/bin/git` is a launcher that cannot run in the sandbox, so before a probe opens the host is asked where the developer tools' git lives, and the probe may read that one git program, which a link in the probe's scratch puts on its `PATH`, git's exec path, its `share/git-core` and its system configuration. The program's neighbours in the developer tools' `usr/bin`, such as its compilers, are neither granted nor on the probe's `PATH`. Where that configuration does not exist the probe's git runs under `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` instead, since the sandbox refuses the absent file's open as not permitted, which git treats as fatal; Melian's own git calls keep that variable, and no other of git's, from the caller's environment. Each but the configuration must lie inside the developer directory, and none may hold or sit inside the reviewer's home; any other answer, or a git before 2.42, leaves git unavailable to probes, and `melian doctor` says so. [The decision](decisions/2026-11-22-probes-run-git-and-workspace-imports.md) records the checks, and the reads the maintainer accepted on 2026-11-22.

A second run on the same file finds the lock and exits 2 before any model, so two runs never save over each other's attempts. A run that died leaves its lock, so its resume exits 2 too, naming the lock and the process ID. The refusal reads the process ID only from a regular file that reads whole as a run's claim, and never follows a link; a lock path that is a link, a directory or a file of other text gets a refusal that quotes nothing from it. No run removes another's lock, so once you know that process is gone, delete `<results>.lock` by hand, as `rm <results>.lock`, and run again. Delete a lock only once its run is gone. A run checks its claim and then saves, so if you delete a live run's lock and a second run takes it in between, the first can still save over the second's results or remove its lock. A hard link to a held results file is a second name the lock does not see, so two runs can start and pay twice. A lock replaced by something that is not a regular file while its run is going can block that run's next save.
